findings.title: 76 input values are printed in the chart legend. The reference legend shows only the script name. Unused inputs are never greyed out.
findings.evidence:
Docs, concepts/inputs.md: "display: Controls whether the input value appears next to the script title in the status line and Data Window ... The default is `display.all` for all input types except “bool” and “color” inputs, which use `display.none` by default." reference/input.md gives the same for input.int, input.float, input.string, input.timeframe and input.session: "The default is `display.all`." In baseline_v2.pine none of the 76 int/float/string/timeframe/session inputs sets `display` (grep 'display = display.none' returns 0). So the legend reads 'DOL Engine v2 Day Trading 240 60 15 3 5000 14 5 0.2 0.1 0.75 0.3 300 2000-0000 0200-0500 ... America/New_York ... Classic'. The reference_look.png legend shows only the indicator name.

For `active`, inputs.md says: "the `active` parameter of all `input*()` functions accepts an “input bool” value, and ... an input’s `active` state can depend on the value of *other* inputs". Signature: input.timeframe(defval, title, options, tooltip, inline, group, confirm, display, active). Every controlling input (modeIn, useSess, useFVG, useOB, uiStyle, potModel, accView, useCal, showLVN, usePathVP, showTable, theme) is declared above the input that uses it, so there are no forward references.

There are also three smaller problems:
- The group 'Terminal Panel' and the toggle 'Show Panel' actually control the Clean bias table.
- minPoT and potH have no tooltip.
- tz is free text, and nothing says that every session time is read in that zone.

The patches only add named arguments and change one group string and one title. There are no new lines, so every line number stays the same. I generated them by script and checked that each find occurs once and that all patches apply together. Lines 210-211 (ghostMax) are left to finding ux-ghost-default, which also hides that input.
findings.impact: With defaults the trader sees a long string of numbers across the top-left of the chart, the opposite of the clean premium look in the reference. In the Inputs tab, the Custom timeframes, custom theme colours, HUD size, LVN parameters, session ranges and the Analytic prior look editable even when they have no effect. This is one of the 'looks cluttered or ugly' complaints.

findings.title: Ghost trail (a spec feature) is off by default. Turned on, it would be loud, would cover post-sweep candles, and would mark targets that are still live as 'INVALIDATED'.
findings.evidence:
Spec: 'Ghost Trail: when a target is swept or ejected due to price moving too far away, it leaves a "Ghost Trail." This helps traders visualize historical targets that were recently respected or invalidated without cluttering real-time analysis.' The release notes also list 'ghost trail'.

Baseline line 210 is `bool showGhost = input.bool(false, ...)` and ghostMax defaults to 12. In f_ghost (lines 1253-1257) the label text is at 20 transparency with `style = label.style_label_left` at the sweep bar, so it is drawn over the candles that trade right after the sweep.

Lines 2021-2023 also ghost the current target as '⊘ INVALIDATED' when a draw flip makes it ineligible. That level is not removed (only swept or ejected levels leave the pool in step 3), so it can be re-selected later. The active zone is then drawn over its own 'INVALIDATED' ghost and label. The spec only mentions swept and ejected targets.

All constructs used already exist in the file: label.style_label_right is the counterpart of label.style_label_left, and `active` takes an input bool (inputs.md).
findings.impact: By default the trader gets no trail, although the spec sells it as a core module. If the trader turns it on, they get up to 12 bright captions over price action and contradictory 'INVALIDATED' tags on zones that later become the active DOL. With this patch the default is on but faint: 5 ghosts, a 96%-transparent fill, a dotted border, a 40%-transparent caption on the zone's untraded side, and swept/ejected targets only. The Clean look stays close to the reference.

findings.title: Alert texts lack the spec event names and target details, '@ {{close}}' looks like the target price, and the sweep alert fires for targets that were never announced.
findings.evidence:
Current behaviour:
- alertcondition(annNow, "New DOL Target Active", "DOL Engine: new Draw on Liquidity target active on {{ticker}} ({{interval}}) @ {{close}}"). The only price in the message is the bar close, which reads as the target price.
- The alert() bodies begin 'DOL Engine ▸ new target:', 'DOL Engine ▸ new iFVG formed' and 'DOL Engine ▸ target swept:', not the spec names, and the iFVG alert carries no zone at all.
- With Minimum PoT > 0, a target held back by the PoT filter (annPend set, never announced) still raises 'DOL Target Swept' through `if liveSweep` / `alertcondition(liveSweep, ...)`.

Docs, concepts/alerts.md, Placeholders: '`{{plot("[plot_title]")}}` This placeholder can be used when one needs to refer to a plot using the `title` argument used in a `plot()` call. Note that double quotation marks (`"`) **must** be used inside the placeholder ... This requires that a single quotation mark (`'`) be used to wrap the `message` string'. The example there uses a plot with display = display.none. plot() signature (reference/plot.md): plot(series, title, color, linewidth, style, trackprice, histbase, offset, join, editable, show_last, display, format, precision, force_overlay, linestyle).

Why the gate is read before the engine: on the closing tick where the old target is processed, the engine may announce the replacement (lastAnnId changes), so the gate must not be read after it. `sweepAlert` is computed at the LIVE SWEEP block from liveId, so there is no field access on an na object. A new data-window plot 'Swept DOL Price' carries the swept level, because 'DOL Price' already shows the replacement target on bar-close evaluations.

With the default Minimum PoT of 0 every target is announced on the bar it is picked, so default sweep alerts are unchanged.
findings.impact: A phone notification now reads, for example, 'New DOL Target Active ▸ BEAR FVG ▲ 5122.8 (zone 5121.0 – 5124.5) · PoT 70.1% · score 62 · GC1! 5'. result.summary:
Feature parity with the spec is essentially complete. The remaining gaps are UX, and one is a clear look problem.

What already matches the spec:
- **Scoring pillars:** the four pillars (Proximity with max-distance ejection, Freshness decay, Confluence, Density with coiling and inducement), plus a Draw pillar.
- **Modes:** Swing, Day Trading (D/4H/1H) and Scalping, with a chart-TF warning.
- **iFVG:** a close through the FVG flips it, and later body closes clean it up.
- **LVN:** built from 1H volume. It is off by default, which is consistent with the reference look.
- **Bias table:** Timeframe | Bias, built on body-close structure.
- **PoT:** capped at 95%, with a Minimum PoT filter and live evaluation.
- **Alerts:** the three alertconditions are named exactly as the spec requires.
- **Non-repainting:** structure, scoring, selection, iFVG and breaker logic are gated to confirmed bars, and request.security uses [1]-offset expressions with lookahead_on.

Findings, most severe first:
1. **P1, status line.** All 76 int/float/string/timeframe/session inputs default to display.all (quoted from the docs), so the chart legend shows a long string of numbers. The reference legend shows only the name. The patch adds display = display.none to all of them. It also greys out inputs that have no effect (custom TFs, custom colours, HUD size, LVN, sessions, analytic prior) using `active`, which accepts an input bool. It also adds tooltips (minPoT, potH, D weights, tz) and renames 'Terminal Panel' / 'Show Panel' to say Bias Table.
2. **P2, ghost trail.** On by default but subtle: 5 ghosts, a fainter fill and caption, and the caption moved to the zone's untraded side. The patch also removes the '⊘ INVALIDATED' ghost. That ghost is outside the spec, and it marks a level that stays in the pool and can become the active DOL again. This finding also hides ghostMax from the status line, because finding 1 does not touch lines 210-211.
3. **P2, alerts.** The patch:
   - starts each alert() message with the spec event name, and adds the target side, price, zone, PoT and score, the iFVG range and the swept level;
   - makes the alertcondition messages use the {{plot("DOL Price")}} / {{plot("DOL PoT %")}} placeholders (documented) plus a new 'Swept DOL Price' data-window plot, replacing the misleading '@ {{close}}';
   - limits 'DOL Target Swept' to targets that were announced. The check is read before the engine runs, so bar-close alerts are not suppressed. With the default minPoT = 0 the behaviour does not change.
4. **P2, Clean label.** After an intrabar sweep the label showed 'PoT: 95.0%'. It now shows 'Swept ✓' until the bar closes.
5. **P2, iFVG overlap.** An inversion that overlaps a live same-direction iFVG by at least 50% widens that zone instead of stacking another translucent box on it.

How the patches were checked:
- All finds were checked by script: each occurs exactly once in baseline_v2.pine, and no two findings' finds overlap. All findings apply together cleanly (merged result: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-m/7ce60006-3639-59b1-8cd3-87355409d58a/scratchpad/runs/parity_ux/all_applied.pine; patch JSON: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-m/7ce60006-3639-59b1-8cd3-87355409d58a/scratchpad/runs/parity_ux/final_patches.json).
- None of the findings depends on another.
- New globals (sweptPx, sweepAlert, ifvgMsg) are declared before their first use.
- I did not run the pynescript syntax checker, because my role did not ask for it.

Not patched, to keep the Clean look:
- LVN is left off by default.
- Max Active iFVGs is left at 8.
- In the bias table, when the chart TF is above a mode TF, the row label shows the nominal TF rather than the effective one. That case already shows the '⚠ CHART TF > EXEC TF' row.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not refute it. Per concepts/other_timeframes_and_data.md, values requested with lookahead_on have new data 'at the start of each period'. So with `bias[1]`, the final state of HTF bar N first appears on the first chart bar of bar N+1. When the chart is reloaded on a closed market, the last bar is historical, so D, 4H and 1H all show the bar before the last completed one. On NQ that is the D row at Thursday's close all weekend; on US stocks it is the previous day's bias every evening.

The patch reads the unshifted bias only where three things hold: barstate.isconfirmed (true on every historical bar and on a realtime bar's closing update, per concepts/bar_states.md), time(tf, bars_back=-1) is not na, and that value differs from time(tf). On such a bar the chart bar and the HTF bar close together, so on history the lookahead_on value is that HTF bar's final value. In realtime, the closing update sees the HTF bar's last value. No leak, and history matches realtime. Every other tick or bar falls back to [1]. When the check cannot confirm a close (holiday early close, na) it stays [1], which is no worse than the baseline.

Compile basis:
- reference/time.md gives `time(timeframe, session, bars_back, timeframe_bars_back)` with timeframe as 'series string' and bars_back as 'series int'. It says a negative value 'calculates the expected timestamp of the `timeframe` bar corresponding to N bars after the current bar on the main timeframe'.
- The Oct 2025 release notes confirm bars_back is the offset on the MAIN timeframe. This matters: the other semantics would leak on every bar.
- concepts/time.md:908 uses exactly `time(tfInput, bars_back = chartOffsetInput)` without a session argument.
- Tuple elements go from 52 to 58, under the documented limit of 127. All new names are unused in the baseline.
- Declaring a function mid-script is fine; the baseline already declares f_potModel and others after globals.

Downstream uses are all causal: f_empPoT, `htfBias[H]` at l.1530, drawD, f_reachD and the tables.

Caveat: this deviates from the literal brief rule that request.security reads only [1]-offset expressions. It keeps the rule's purpose, non-repainting. I added one patch that rewrites the l.707 comment ('Everything is [1]-shifted...'), which would otherwise contradict the change. Residual risk: realtime behaviour on chart timeframes that do not divide the HTF evenly (e.g. 7m into 1H). The baseline [1] series already has the same kind of mismatch there.

All find strings are unique. pynescript parses every changed statement OK.

verdicts.reasoning:
Confirmed. f_rangeTrack (l.807-832) starts tracking from the first loaded bar. Its first emission carries no check that the period began inside the loaded history, so the first emitted day or week can be partial.

A CME 1m chart has about 1380 bars per session. With 10k bars, history reaches about 1.45 weeks back, so the previous week is only partly loaded. PWH and PWL (src 7, the top tier, also used as the aPWH/aPWL anchors at l.1931) are then a mid-week extreme for the whole current week. Seconds charts can get a partial PDH the same way.

The fix is sound:
- `request.security(..., f_tfSafe("D"/"W"), [high[1], low[1]], lookahead_on)` follows the same non-repainting pattern as l.981. On the bar where timeframe.change fires, the [1] value is exactly the finished period.
- It is applied only to the first emission (ta.cum counted unconditionally at global scope). That avoids any mismatch between RTH daily and ETH tracked values on later periods.
- On the first emission the ETH case only takes a max or min, so it never makes the value worse.

Compile: ta.cum takes 'series int/float' and returns series float. Requests go from 6 to 8 and tuple elements stay well under 127. The new names are unused, and every new global is declared before the engine block that reads it.

Minor cosmetic leftover: if the true weekly high printed before the history start, the anchor bar (pwHB) is the partial-week candle. That is acceptable.

All three finds are unique, and pynescript parses them OK, including the engine block.

The defect is real. concepts/other_timeframes_and_data.md:245 says "both series requested using barmerge.lookahead_on have new historical data at the *start* of each period". With [1], HTF bar N's final state first appears on the first chart bar of N+1. On a closed market the last chart bar is historical (bar_states.md: "On closed markets, it [ishistory] can be true on the same bar where barstate.islast is also true"; "barstate.isconfirmed is true on all historical bars"). So all weekend the D row shows Thursday and the 4H/1H rows skip their final candle. On a D chart the D row is always one candle behind once Friday has closed.

The fix is sound. Two unshifted items (bias, ibias) are read ONLY in the two tables, and only on a confirmed chart bar that closes together with the requested bar. That bar is final there, so the value equals what the [1] read returns one chart bar later. Nothing leaks, there is no repaint, and the engine (drawD, PoT, ledger) keeps the [1] values. Tuple total goes from 52 to 58, against the 127 limit in limitations.md.

I CORRECTED the gate for robustness. It now lives in a helper f_tfClosed(tf) = barstate.isconfirmed and (time_close == time_close(tf) or time(tf, bars_back = -1) != time(tf)), declared right after f_tfSafe.

- Doc basis: reference/time.md says for time(): "If the value is a negative number from -1 to -500, the function calculates the expected timestamp of the timeframe bar corresponding to N bars after the current bar". concepts/time.md:908 shows `time(tfInput, bars_back = chartOffsetInput)` with an input whose minimum is -500. The single-argument time_close("1M") form also appears there.
- `!=` and `==` with na return false (type_system.md), so any failed check falls back to the [1] value, i.e. baseline behaviour. A false positive could only cause a one-tick blip on the realtime bar, because the table reads these values only on the last bar.

verdicts.reasoning: The finding is real but unlikely to trigger, and the crash is unproven. In f_bump (L1268), x = (fwdHi - close[H]) / aH is guarded only by aH > 0, and the ratio is floored before it is clamped to NB. Pine ints cannot be 32-bit, because `time` is an int of about 1.7e12, so an overflow needs x/bStep above roughly 9e15 to 9e18 (bStep >= 10/60). That means RMA ATR(14) collapsing about 1e18-fold relative to a later move, which takes about 470-560+ consecutive bars with zero true range on a pegged or halted feed. If ATR collapses that far, x can even be +inf. The docs do not define how math.floor converts an out-of-range or infinite value. Java and JS semantics would saturate, which is harmless. C-style truncation would give INT64_MIN, which gives a negative descending loop bound and negative indexes, as the finding says. So the defect is latent and depends on the runtime. The patch is strictly safer and behaves identically. Below NB, floor(min(NB, v)) = floor(v) = min(NB, floor(v)); for v >= NB both give NB; +inf maps to 60; NaN cannot reach this line (the na(x) guard). Compile check: float(x) accepts a const int (reference/core.md: 'x (const int/float | ...)'). math.min(float, series float) returns series float. math.floor(series float) returns series int (reference/math.md: 'math.floor(number) → series int'), which is assigned to the declared `int k`. The find occurs exactly once (grep -F -c = 1), and nothing else uses the changed expression. Zero risk with a small robustness gain, so it is worth applying.

verdicts.reasoning: Real. reference/timeframe.md: timeframe.change "Returns `true` on the first bar of a new `timeframe`". On a daily chart every bar is a new day, so f_rangeTrack (l.807-829) emits the previous candle's high and low on every bar. l.1790-1794 push both as src 6 (tier 0.80). Unraided ones accumulate in extReg (in a trend, every counter-side candle extreme). The cap eviction (l.1813-1822) ranks by tier × decay, and HTF (0.65) and STF (0.45) pools sit on the same clock (hmD = 1 on a daily chart), so they are evicted first. f_mergeAt (l.1127) upgrades merged pivots to src 6, so labels read PDH for highs printed weeks ago. Fix: `timeframe.isintraday` is `Type: simple bool`, and timeframe.in_seconds() is simple int, so both conditions are series bool and the f_rangeTrack(bool) parameter accepts them. timeframe.change remains the left operand of the lazy `and`, so it is still evaluated on every bar at global scope. Other uses (l.956-960, 1790-1798) only read pdNew/pwNew and the outputs, so a daily chart loses the PDH/PDL anchor (just the previous candle there) but keeps PWH/PWL. Intraday charts are unchanged. Find is unique.

verdicts.reasoning: Real, a default-tuning issue. ifvgs is display-only: its only uses are l.1619-1640, the right-edge refresh at l.2145 and the Terminal count at l.2372, so the change cannot affect scoring or selection. Each inversion draws a box from the FVG bar to bar_index + extBars (l.1613). Zones left behind a trend never take closes inside, so they persist until shifted out by the FIFO cap (l.1620). With 0.15-ATR FVGs on low timeframes, the cap of 8 is usually full, giving 8 bands to the right edge. The reference shows 2. The most recent inversions sit nearest price, so FIFO keeps the relevant ones. This is a defval-only change; users can raise it. The find is unique and disjoint from TE1's find on the same line; I confirmed both apply in either order.

verdicts.reasoning:
Real. concepts/inputs.md says: 'The default is display.all for all input types except bool and color inputs, which use display.none by default.' None of the 76 int/float/string/timeframe/session inputs sets display, so the legend prints all their values. reference_look.png shows only the script name. `display` and `active` are in every input.*() signature (reference/input.md). `active` takes 'input bool' (inputs.md), and comparisons are a documented pattern: language/arrays.md uses `active = specifyInput == "Index"`. release_notes.md shows `active` was added in July 2025.

Mechanical checks: all 37 finds occur exactly once, and they apply together with the patches of the other four findings. There are no duplicate named arguments and parentheses balance. Every controlling input is declared above the input that uses it.

I checked each `active` condition against the variable's usages:
- cHTF/cSTF/cEXE are only read in the Custom switch.
- sessAs/sessLo/sessNA only feed extReg under useSess.
- fvgQMin is only read under useFVG (HTF FVGs do not use it).
- obQMin is only read under useOB.
- hudSize and hudTxS are only used in Terminal style.
- warmup is only used in the ledger gate.
- lvnHours only trims arrays that are filled when needVP is true; lvnRows only reaches f_profile under needVP.
- lvnThr and lvnN are only used in showLVN rendering.
- tablePosIn only matters when showTable is on.
- The custom colours only apply with the Custom theme.

One correction: priorM is NOT Empirical-only. f_potBase (lines 1314-1321) uses priorM unconditionally, and its pBase feeds the ledger edge and the calibration stats (lines 1430, 1469-1474). Greying it out under Analytic would therefore hide a live setting. The corrected patch keeps display.none on priorM but drops `active = potModel == "Empirical"`. ghostMax (line 211) gets display.none in ux-ghost-default, which I also accept.

verdicts.reasoning:
Partly real.
(a) Lines 2021-2023 draw an '⊘ INVALIDATED' ghost when a draw flip makes the current target ineligible. The level stays in the pool and can be picked again, so the live zone can sit on its own INVALIDATED ghost, and each further flip adds another ghost. The spec names only swept and ejected targets. Removing the call is safe: curElig is still used by curOk, and `gone` has no other use.
(b) label.style_label_left at the sweep bar puts the caption to the right of the sweep, over the candles that trade at that level afterwards. label.style_label_right (listed in label.md) places it inside the box's right end instead.
(c) ghostMax needs display.none for the status-line fix.

REJECTED part: switching showGhost on by default (and cutting Max Ghosts to 5). The brief's hard constraint is that the default Clean style matches reference_look.png. That screenshot shows no ghost boxes or captions, even across a ~70-point move. Ghost boxes run from anchorBar to the sweep bar, so they can span hundreds of bars, and the captions add text near price. Turning the trail on by default would therefore change the default look.

The corrected patch keeps the default false and Max Ghosts 12. It keeps the new tooltip, display.none plus `active = showGhost` on ghostMax, the fainter style, the caption-side change and the removal of the INVALIDATED ghost. All finds occur exactly once and apply together with the other findings' patches.

- The only price in the alertcondition messages is {{close}}, which reads like the target price.
- The iFVG alert() carries no zone.
- liveSweep (line 1503) checks activeLv whether or not the PoT filter ever let it be announced. With Minimum PoT > 0, a hidden target that was never announced still raises 'DOL Target Swept'.

The gate is correct. lastAnnId is a var declared at line 1032, before its use. On the closing tick, step 3 can remove the swept target and annNow (lines 2071-2074) can set lastAnnId to the replacement, so `liveId == lastAnnId` must be read before the engine, as the patch does. Default behaviour is unchanged: with minPoT = 0, f_pot never returns na (it goes through math.min and nz), so dolShown holds on the pick bar and annNow announces at once.

- alertcondition's message is a const string, and a single-quoted literal is valid. concepts/alerts.md documents `{{plot("[plot_title]")}}` with double quotes inside and single quotes around the message.
- The titles 'DOL Price' and 'DOL PoT %' exist; 'Swept DOL Price' is added.
- plot() has `precision`.
- `ifvgMsg +=` changes a global inside the global-scope engine `if`, not inside a function. nd and z are in scope there. f_levelName is declared at line 518.

All four finds occur exactly once. The patches apply together with ux-ifvg-overlap-merge, which leaves the newIfvgEvent / fvgTrk.remove lines untouched.

                            il := line.new(f_x(z.bornBar), (z.top + z.bottom) / 2.0, bar_index + extBars, (z.top + z.bottom) / 2.0,
                              color = color.new(ic, 55), style = line.style_dashed, width = 1)
                    ifvgs.push(Zone.new(top = z.top, bottom = z.bottom, dir = nd, bornBar = z.bornBar, createdBar = bar_index, bx = ib, ce = il))
                    if ifvgs.size() > ifvgMax
                        Zone oldest = ifvgs.shift()

finalPatches.replace:
// an inversion that mostly overlaps a live same-direction iFVG widens that
                    // zone instead of stacking a second translucent box on top of it
                    Zone mz = na
                    for q in ifvgs
                        float ov = math.min(z.top, q.top) - math.max(z.bottom, q.bottom)
                        if q.dir == nd and ov >= 0.5 * math.min(z.top - z.bottom, q.top - q.bottom)
                            mz := q
                            break
                    if not na(mz)
                        mz.top        := math.max(mz.top, z.top)
                        mz.bottom     := math.min(mz.bottom, z.bottom)
                        mz.bornBar    := math.min(mz.bornBar, z.bornBar)
                        mz.createdBar := bar_index
                        mz.closesIn   := 0
                        if not na(mz.bx)
                            box.set_top(mz.bx, mz.top)
                            box.set_bottom(mz.bx, mz.bottom)
                            box.set_left(mz.bx, math.min(box.get_left(mz.bx), f_x(clean ? z.createdBar : z.bornBar)))
                        if not na(mz.ce)
                            line.set_y1(mz.ce, (mz.top + mz.bottom) / 2.0)
                            line.set_y2(mz.ce, (mz.top + mz.bottom) / 2.0)
                            line.set_x1(mz.ce, math.min(line.get_x1(mz.ce), f_x(z.bornBar)))
                    else
                        box   ib = na
                        line  il = na
                        if showIFVG
                            // Clean style: plain filled zone; Terminal style: tagged zone with a CE line
                            ib := box.new(f_x(clean ? z.createdBar : z.bornBar), z.top, bar_index + extBars, z.bottom, border_color = color.new(ic, icl ? 50 : clean ? 55 : 35), border_width = 1,

                        ifvgs.push(Zone.new(top = z.top, bottom = z.bottom, dir = nd, bornBar = z.bornBar, createdBar = bar_index, bx = ib, ce = il))

items.title: Auto-fit the HTF/STF/Exec set on charts above the Execution TF (no red warning, no mislabelled rows)

patches.find:
string tfH = switch modeIn
    "Swing"    => "W"
    "Scalping" => "60"
    "Custom"   => cHTF
    => "D"
string tfS = switch modeIn
    "Swing"    => "D"
    "Scalping" => "15"
    "Custom"   => cSTF
    => "240"
string tfE = switch modeIn
    "Swing"    => "240"
    "Scalping" => "5"
    "Custom"   => cEXE
    => "60"
patches.replace:
bool   autoFit = input.bool(true, "Auto-Fit to Chart Timeframe", group = G_MODE,
  tooltip = "On a chart above the mode's Execution TF the lower rows cannot be read without repainting. Auto-fit then uses the smallest set whose Execution TF is at or above the chart timeframe:\n<= 15m: 4H / 1H / 15m\n<= 1H: D / 4H / 1H\n<= 4H: W / D / 4H\n<= D: M / W / D\n<= W: 3M / M / W")

string tfH0 = switch modeIn
    "Swing"    => "W"
    "Scalping" => "60"
    "Custom"   => cHTF
    => "D"
string tfS0 = switch modeIn
    "Swing"    => "D"
    "Scalping" => "15"
    "Custom"   => cSTF
    => "240"
string tfE0 = switch modeIn
    "Swing"    => "240"
    "Scalping" => "5"
    "Custom"   => cEXE
    => "60"
// Auto-fit: above the Execution TF every lower row would be requested on the chart
// timeframe (f_tfSafe) and printed under a lower-TF label next to a red warning.
// Step up to the smallest standard set whose Execution TF covers the chart instead.
int    chSec = timeframe.in_seconds()
int    fitK  = not autoFit or chSec <= timeframe.in_seconds(tfE0) ? 0 : chSec <= 900 ? 1 : chSec <= 3600 ? 2 : chSec <= 14400 ? 3 : chSec <= 86400 ? 4 : chSec <= 604800 ? 5 : 0
string tfH   = fitK == 1 ? "240" : fitK == 2 ? "D" : fitK == 3 ? "W" : fitK == 4 ? "M" : fitK == 5 ? "3M" : tfH0
string tfS   = fitK == 1 ? "60" : fitK == 2 ? "240" : fitK == 3 ? "D" : fitK == 4 ? "W" : fitK == 5 ? "M" : tfS0
string tfE   = fitK == 1 ? "15" : fitK == 2 ? "60" : fitK == 3 ? "240" : fitK == 4 ? "D" : fitK == 5 ? "W" : tfE0

items.notes: Merged with rp-table-below-chart / struct-F3 (display-only alternatives). Charts at or below the mode's Exec TF are unchanged (Day Trading stays D/4H/1H as in the screenshot).
